title: French Defense: Winawer Variation
line: The bishop pins the knight, and Black gives it up to double White's pawns.

steps.text: In the French, White's knight came out to guard the pawn on e4.
Bring the bishop to b4. It pins the knight that guards e4.

also.g8f6: That is the Classical Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Winawer.
also.d5e4: That is the Rubinstein Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Winawer.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c7 two squares to hit the base of White's chain.
steps.after: White asks the bishop to decide.

steps.text: Take the knight with the bishop, with check.

also.b4a5: That keeps the bishop, and it is also played. This lesson takes the knight.

steps.text: Two white pawns now stand on one file, one in front of the other. Tap both of them.
steps.after: Doubled pawns are slow and hard to guard. In return, White keeps both bishops.

steps.text: Bring the knight to e7. On f6 White's pawn would kick it.
Bring the queen to a5. She hits the weak pawn on c3 and pins it to White's king.
steps.after: White guards it with a bishop.

summary: In the Winawer, Black gives a bishop for a knight to double White's pawns, then attacks the weak ones.
